answer: To enforce Sybil resistance, recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind to sequential delay functions, forcing attackers to mirror state history across a cryptographic trellis of verifier nodes. Attempting to forge identities triggers immediate slashing of staking collateral, proving a negative expected utility. By combining zero-knowledge verifiable delay with these slashing penalties, the system secures a Nash equilibrium where cloning incurs insurmountable computational costs.
